result.reason: The Mishna text introduces the three-brothers scenario with two sisters and one unrelated woman, which is precisely what the 'Three Brothers Setup' section's prose describes as its content.

The passage contains both the deduction about 'died first then divorced' implying a problem (which sets up the zika discussion) AND Rav Ashi's explicit conclusion that 'yesh zika afilu bitrei achai' — matching exactly the prose of candidate 2 ('Rav Ashi vs Rav Nachman') which directly discusses Rav Ashi's inference of zika even with two brothers.

Both items contain Rav Ashi's direct response explaining that the Mishnah mentioned ma'amar to exclude Beit Shammai's view of full kinyan, not because ma'amar was necessary to create the prohibition — exactly what the 'Ashi's Response' prose describes.

All five items are a continuous Gemara discussion about what the Mishnah's phrase 'this is' (זו היא) excludes according to Rav Nachman vs. Rav Ashi vs. Rava, which is precisely what heading 0 ('Nachman's Exclusion') describes — asking 'zu le-ma'utei mai' and analyzing the three possible sequences of events, whereas the current placement under heading 1 ('Nishuin/Mita Debate') describes the downstream conclusion about nishuin rishonim vs. mita mappelet that emerges from that analysis.

The passage introduces the Mishnah's rule that uncertain betrothal/divorce cases require chalitza but not yibbum, which is precisely what the 'Safek Principle' section describes — the general category and ruling — before the specific illustration of safek kiddushin is elaborated in candidate 3.

The passage directly quotes the three types of defective gittin (written in his handwriting with no witnesses, witnesses but no date, date but only one witness) which is precisely what the 'Safek Gerushin' prose section describes and analyzes.

Both items together form the Gemara's observation about the missing parallel case in divorce and Rabba's answer explaining why — exactly what the 'Missing Parallel' prose describes, including the asymmetry question and the chazakah-based resolution.

The passage is Abaye's challenge applying the same chazakah logic to kiddushin, which is exactly what 'Challenge to Logic' describes — pressing Rava's reasoning with 'i hachi be-kiddushin nami neima.'

The entire passage covers the cost-benefit analysis of the chalitza chumra — the 'chumra de-atya lidei kula' objection and its resolution — which is precisely what candidate 2's prose describes, including the signaling effect of chalitza, the 'midei yada de-chumra be-alma' reasoning, and the conclusion that even mistaken yibbum would not be a real violation due to presumptive status.

The passage is the Mishnah citation from Abaye's objection — the building falling on the man and his brother's daughter — which is precisely what the 'Setup' section introduces as the new case Abaye brings to challenge Rava.

The passage asks why we don't apply the presumptive permitted status to avoid rendering the rival wife forbidden due to uncertainty — this is directly about the uncertainty dilemma introduced in candidate 0, before the Mishnah's solution is presented.

The passage directly contains the Gemara's resolution about frequency (gerushin de-shkhikhei/mapoles de-lo shkhikhei), which is precisely what the 'Frequency Principle' prose section explains and analyzes.
